reading: A red band at the top has holes; grey pieces lie at the bottom. Each grey piece is lifted into the hole whose shape it matches (fitting the red band like a jigsaw) and turns blue; the bottom is cleared.

slots.pieces: grey (5) objects in the lower half
slots.holes: background notches in the bottom edge of the red band
slots.match: piece shape equals hole shape (piece pushed up until it fills the notch)
slots.colour: pieces become 1 at their new place; old places cleared

why: every hole is exactly filled by one piece of the same shape, recoloured 1

reading: The output is the red square outline cut out, with the small 3x3 coloured shape scaled up by an integer factor to exactly fill the outline's interior.

slots.frame: the red (2) square outline object; output = its box

why: output is the frame box and its interior equals the shape upscaled by interior_size/3

reading: Every 3x3 hollow square of 1s is replaced by a red plus (corners become background); other shapes stay.

new_rows.name: ring_centre
new_rows.datalog:
fgc(Y, X) :- cell(Y, X, C).
nb(Y, X, count(DY, DX)) :- px(Y, X, C), !fgc(Y, X), off(DY, DX), Y2 = Y + DY, X2 = X + DX, fgc(Y2, X2).
ring_centre(Y, X) :- nb(Y, X, N), N = 8.

why: at each background cell whose 8 neighbours are all foreground, the 3x3 block becomes 020/222/020

reading: Objects of 4 or more cells fall straight down until they touch the bottom border; small objects (1-3 cells) stay where they are.

new_rows.name: big
new_rows.datalog:
osize(O, count(Y, X)) :- obj(O, Y, X).
big(Y, X) :- obj(O, Y, X), osize(O, N), N > 3.

why: each big object keeps its shape and column and its lowest cell ends on the bottom row; small objects unchanged

reading: Every 3x3 square made entirely of 0 is filled with 1; when two such squares overlap, only the first in reading order is filled.

new_rows.name: sq3
new_rows.datalog:
z(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, 0).
sq(Y, X) :- z(Y, X), Y1 = Y + 1, Y2 = Y + 2, X1 = X + 1, X2 = X + 2, z(Y, X1), z(Y, X2), z(Y1, X), z(Y1, X1), z(Y1, X2), z(Y2, X), z(Y2, X1), z(Y2, X2).
earlier(Y, X) :- sq(Y, X), sq(A, B), A < Y, DA = Y - A, DA <= 2, DB = X - B, DB <= 2, DB >= -2.
earlier(Y, X) :- sq(Y, X), sq(Y, B), B < X, DB = X - B, DB <= 2.
pick(Y, X) :- sq(Y, X), !earlier(Y, X).
sq3(Y, X) :- pick(A, B), Y = A + 1, X = B + 1.
sq3(Y, X) :- pick(A, B), off(DY, DX), Y = A + 1 + DY, X = B + 1 + DX.

why: exactly the cells of the chosen all-0 3x3 squares become 1

reading: The grid is 3x3 panels cut by grey lines. The panel containing a yellow 4 is copied into the panel slot given by the 4's position inside its panel; all other panels are cleared.

slots.target: panel at (row, col) = position of the 4 within the source panel
slots.rest: all other panel cells set to 0

why: output panel at the 4's local position equals the source panel; every other panel is empty

reading: A large umbrella shape sits among scattered single cells. Each single cell lying below the umbrella in a column it covers draws a vertical line of its colour from just under the umbrella down to the bottom border.

new_rows.name: under
new_rows.datalog:
osize(O, count(Y, X)) :- obj(O, Y, X).
under(Y, X) :- obj(M, Y, X), osize(M, N), N = 1, obj(U, Y2, X), osize(U, K), K > 1, Y2 < Y.

why: each such column is filled with the marker colour from the cell below the umbrella to the bottom row; umbrella untouched

reading: The output is a 3x3 pattern of 5 chosen by the number of colours in the input: 1 colour gives a full top row, 2 colours the main diagonal, 3 colours the anti-diagonal.

slots.count: number of distinct colours in the input

why: output equals the pattern indexed by the input's colour count

reading: Each L-shaped three-cell object shoots a diagonal line of its colour from its missing corner outward (away from the object, starting one cell beyond the missing corner) to the grid border.

new_rows.name: ray_start
new_rows.datalog:
diag(DY, DX) :- off(DY, DX), P = DY * DX, P = 1.
diag(DY, DX) :- off(DY, DX), P = DY * DX, P = -1.
ray_start(Y, X) :- diag(DY, DX), px(Ym, Xm, 0), A = Ym + DY, B = Xm + DX, obj(O, A, Xm), obj(O, Ym, B), obj(O, A, B), Y = Ym - DY, X = Xm - DX.

why: each diagonal starts one cell past the L's missing corner, continues in the direction away from the L, and reaches the border; missing corner stays empty

reading: The grid is doubled in width: the input is joined to its left-right mirror image with colours inverted (0 becomes 8, 2 becomes 0); the mirrored copy goes on the side whose edge the red shape touches.

slots.side: copy placed on the side (left/right) where the input's shape touches the edge

why: one half equals the input, the other half equals the inverted mirror, joined at the touched edge
